claims.text: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr is a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Bulk equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits a stable BCC phase.
HfNbTaTiZr has high intrinsic resistance to oxidation and corrosion.
Dealloying and nanostructuring can selectively remove less-active species or create a porous surface in HfNbTaTiZr.
Dealloying HfNbTaTiZr creates nanoscale surface defects and compositional heterogeneity.
The defects and compositional heterogeneity produced by dealloying provide a high density of catalytically active sites.
These microstructural active sites facilitate hydrogen adsorption and hydrogen evolution and oxidation reactions.
The alloy's resistance to oxidative and corrosive degradation improves electrocatalyst durability under harsh electrochemical conditions.
High mixing entropy in the refractory HEA produces complex surface chemistry.
Nanostructure-induced defect sites and heterogeneous elemental distributions reduce the activation energy for HER and HOR.
Dealloyed nanostructured HfNbTaTiZr can exhibit enhanced catalytic activity for both HER and HOR.
The dealloyed HEA will have lower HER and HOR overpotentials than conventional catalysts.
The dealloyed HEA will produce higher HER and HOR current densities than conventional catalysts.
The dealloyed HEA will retain its activity over extended electrochemical cycling.
Commercial Pt and Pt-alloy catalysts have high HER and HOR catalytic activity.
Commercial Pt and Pt-alloy catalysts suffer from high cost and long-term durability limitations under harsh conditions.
The proposed performance gain is expected mainly under moderately severe electrochemical conditions.
Extremely high or low pH or extreme temperatures may alter the proposed advantageous behavior.
